claims.quote: The company shall be advised, in writing, of the time and place of the informal hearing and shall be directed to bring all documents, records and other information as it may find necessary and relevant to support its position.
claims.summary: The company must be advised in writing of the time and place of the informal hearing and must bring relevant documents and information.

claims.quote: The company may be represented by counsel and shall have a fair opportunity to present any relevant material and to examine the administrative record.
claims.summary: The company has the right to be represented by counsel and to present and examine relevant material and the administrative record.

claims.quote: The complaining agency may be requested by the Reviewing Official to send a representative to the hearing to present any relevant material, and the agency representative may examine the administrative record.
claims.summary: The complaining agency may be requested to send a representative to the hearing to present relevant material and examine the administrative record.

claims.quote: The Reviewing Official is authorized to require the submission of additional documentation from the complaining agency and the company to ensure appropriate consideration of relevant factual or legal issues.
claims.summary: The Reviewing Official may require the submission of additional documentation from the complaining agency and the company to ensure appropriate consideration of relevant issues.

claims.quote: Upon completion of the informal hearing, the Review, the Reviewing Official shall prepare a written Recommendation Memorandum addressed to the Deciding Official setting forth findings and a recommended disposition.
claims.summary: The Reviewing Official must prepare a written Recommendation Memorandum addressed to the Deciding Official upon completion of the informal hearing.

claims.quote: The administrative record consists of the Federal agency complaint referenced in paragraphs (a) and (b) of this section, the company response referenced in paragraph (c), any other documentation submitted to, considered by, or entered into the administrative record by the Reviewing Official, the hearing transcript, and the Reviewing Official's Recommendation Memorandum.
claims.summary: The administrative record includes the Federal agency complaint, company response, other documentation submitted, the hearing transcript, and the Reviewing Official's Recommendation Memorandum.

claims.quote: If, after one year from the date that Treasury notifies the company of its decision to decline to renew or revoke the certificate of authority of a company under this part, the company can demonstrate that the basis for the non-renewal or revocation has been cured, as determined by Treasury in its discretion, and that it can comply with, and does meet, all continuing requirements for certification under 31.U.S.C. 9304-9308 and this part, the company may submit an application to Treasury for reinstatement or reissuance of a certificate of authority, which will be granted without prejudice if all such requirements are met.
claims.summary: A company may submit an application for reinstatement or reissuance of a certificate of authority if it can demonstrate that the basis for non-renewal or revocation has been cured and it meets all continuing requirements.

claims.quote: Treasury may waive the one year waiting period for good cause shown, as determined by Treasury in its sole discretion.
claims.summary: Treasury may waive the one-year waiting period for reinstatement if good cause is shown.

claims.quote: Fees shall be imposed and collected, for the services listed in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of this section that are performed by Treasury, regardless of whether the action requested is granted or denied.
claims.summary: Fees must be imposed and collected for the services listed in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of this section that are performed by Treasury, regardless of whether the action requested is granted or denied.

claims.quote: In a given year a uniform fee will be collected from every company requesting a particular category of service, e.g., determination of a company's continuing qualifications for annual renewal of its certificate of authority.
claims.affected_party: companies requesting a particular category of service
claims.summary: A uniform fee must be collected from every company requesting a particular category of service in a given year.

claims.quote: Fees are determined in accordance with Office of Management and Budget Circular A-25, as amended.
claims.summary: Fees must be determined in accordance with Office of Management and Budget Circular A-25, as amended.

claims.quote: Specific fee information may be obtained from the Surety Bonds Program, or online at https://www.fiscal.treasury.gov/files/surety-bonds/user-fees.pdf.
claims.summary: Specific fee information must be obtained from the Surety Bonds Program or online at the provided URL.

claims.quote: A notice of the amount of a fee referred to in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of this section will be published in the Federal Register as each change in such fee is made.
claims.summary: A notice of the amount of a fee referred to in paragraphs (a)(1) through (6) of this section must be published in the Federal Register as each change in such fee is made.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service may enter into a reciprocal agreement with a State for the collection of past-due support being enforced by the State by administrative offset from certain Federal payments.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must enter into reciprocal agreements with States for the collection of past-due support being enforced by the State by administrative offset from certain Federal payments.

claims.quote: Upon notification of past-due support either directly from a State which has entered into such an agreement or from HHS, disbursing officials of Fiscal Service or any other disbursing official of the United States shall offset Federal payments which are subject to offset under this section, to collect past-due support.
claims.affected_party: disbursing officials of Fiscal Service and any other disbursing official of the United States
claims.summary: Disbursing officials of Fiscal Service or any other disbursing official of the United States must offset Federal payments subject to offset under this section to collect past-due support upon notification.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service may enter into reciprocal agreements with States for disbursing officials of Fiscal Service and any other Federal disbursing official to offset certain Federal payments to collect past-due support being enforced by the State.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must enter into reciprocal agreements with States for disbursing officials of Fiscal Service and any other Federal disbursing official to offset certain Federal payments to collect past-due support being enforced by the State.

claims.quote: The agreement shall contain any requirements which Fiscal Service considers appropriate to facilitate the offset and prevent duplicative efforts and shall require States to prescribe procedures governing the collection of past-due support by Federal administrative offset.
claims.summary: The agreement must contain requirements that Fiscal Service considers appropriate to facilitate the offset and prevent duplicative efforts, and States must prescribe procedures governing the collection of past-due support by Federal administrative offset.

claims.quote: States which have entered into an agreement with Fiscal Service pursuant to this section may thereafter request, in the manner prescribed herein, that an offset be performed.
claims.summary: States that have entered into an agreement with Fiscal Service pursuant to this section must request, in the manner prescribed herein, that an offset be performed.

claims.quote: States notifying Fiscal Service of past-due support must do so in the manner and format prescribed by Fiscal Service. States notifying HHS of past-due support must do so in the manner and format prescribed by HHS.
claims.summary: States must notify Fiscal Service or HHS of past-due support in the manner and format prescribed by the respective agency.

claims.quote: HHS shall notify Fiscal Service of all past-due support referred to HHS by States for collection by administrative offset provided that the requirements of paragraphs (d)(3) and (h) of this section have been met.
claims.summary: HHS must notify Fiscal Service of all past-due support referred to HHS by States for collection by administrative offset, provided the requirements of paragraphs (d)(3) and (h) are met.

claims.quote: When a State has knowledge that past-due support is being enforced by more than one State, the State notifying Fiscal Service or HHS of the past-due support must inform any other State involved in enforcing the past-due support when it refers the debt for offset and when it receives the offset amount.
claims.summary: If a State knows that past-due support is being enforced by more than one State, it must inform any other State involved in enforcing the past-due support when it refers the debt for offset and when it receives the offset amount.

claims.quote: The notification of past-due support must be accompanied by a certification that the debt is past-due, legally enforceable, and that the State has complied with all the requirements as set forth in paragraph (h) of this section and with any requirements imposed by State law or procedure.
claims.summary: The notification of past-due support must be accompanied by a certification that the debt is past-due, legally enforceable, and that the State has complied with all the requirements as set forth in paragraph (h) of this section and with any requirements imposed by State law or procedure.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service may reject a notification of past-due support which does not comply with the requirements of this section. The State will be notified of the rejection along with the reason for the rejection.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service may reject a notification of past-due support that does not comply with the requirements of this section, and the State will be notified of the rejection along with the reason for the rejection.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will reject a notification of past-due support where the past-due support owed is less than $25.00. This amount may be adjusted from time to time by Fiscal Service to ensure that the cost of collection does not exceed the debt.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service will reject a notification of past-due support where the past-due support owed is less than $25.00. This amount may be adjusted from time to time by Fiscal Service to ensure that the cost of collection does not exceed the debt.

claims.quote: The State notifying Fiscal Service or HHS of past-due support shall, in the manner and in the time frames provided by Fiscal Service or HHS, notify Fiscal Service or HHS of deletions or decreases in the amount of a debt referred for collection by administrative offset.
claims.summary: The State notifying Fiscal Service or HHS of past-due support must, in the manner and time frames provided by Fiscal Service or HHS, notify them of deletions or decreases in the amount of a debt referred for collection by administrative offset.

claims.quote: The State may notify Fiscal Service or HHS of any increases in the amount of a debt referred for collection by administrative offset provided the State has complied with the requirements of paragraph (h) of this section with regard to those amounts.
claims.summary: The State may notify Fiscal Service or HHS of any increases in the amount of a debt referred for collection by administrative offset provided the State has complied with the requirements of paragraph (h) of this section with regard to those amounts.

claims.quote: The State, or Fiscal Service or HHS on behalf of the State, if the State requests and Fiscal Service or HHS agrees, shall send a written notification, at least 30 days in advance of referral of the debt for offset, to the individual owing past-due support, informing the individual that the State intends to refer the debt for collection by administrative offset against Federal payments.
claims.summary: The State, or Fiscal Service or HHS on behalf of the State, if the State requests and Fiscal Service or HHS agrees, must send a written notification at least 30 days in advance of referral of the debt for offset to the individual owing past-due support, informing them that the State intends to refer the debt for collection by administrative offset against Federal payments.

claims.quote: Prior to referring a debt to Fiscal Service for collection by administrative offset, States must provide individuals with a reasonable opportunity to exercise the rights enumerated in paragraph (h)(1) of this section in accordance with procedures prescribed by the State.
claims.summary: Prior to referring a debt to Fiscal Service for collection by administrative offset, States must provide individuals with a reasonable opportunity to exercise the rights enumerated in paragraph (h)(1) of this section in accordance with procedures prescribed by the State.

claims.quote: (i) Payments subject to offset. Federal payments subject to offset under this section include all Federal payments except: (1) Payments due to an individual under (i) Title IV of the Higher Education Act of 1965; (ii) The Social Security Act; (iii) Part B of the Black Lung Benefits Act; (iv) Any law administered by the Railroad Retirement Board; (2) Payments which the Secretary determines are exempt from offset in accordance with paragraph (k) of this section; (3) Payments from which collection of past-due support by administrative offset is expressly prohibited by law; (4) Payments made under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 (except that tax refund payments are subject to offset under separate authority); and (5) Payments made under the tariff laws of the United States.
claims.summary: Federal payments subject to offset under this section include all Federal payments except those specified in (1) through (5).

claims.quote: (j) Special provisions applicable to Federal salary payments. (1) Unless a lower maximum offset limitation is provided by applicable State law, the maximum part of a Federal salary payment per pay period subject to offset to collect past-due support shall not exceed those amounts set forth at section 1673(b)(2) (A) and (B) of Title 15, United States Code, as follows: (i) Fifty (50%) percent of the debtor's aggregate disposable earnings for any pay period, where the debtor asserts by affidavit, or by other acceptable evidence, that he/she is supporting a spouse and/or dependent child, other than the former spouse and/or child for whom support is being collected, except that an additional five (5%) percent will apply if it appears that such earnings are to enforce past-due support for a period which is twelve (12) weeks or more prior to the pay period to which the offset applies. A debtor shall be considered to be supporting a spouse and/or dependent child only if the debtor provides over half of the spouse's and/or dependent child's support. (ii) Sixty (60%) percent of the debtor's aggregate disposable earnings for any pay period where the debtor fails to assert by affidavit or establish by other acceptable evidence that he/she is supporting a spouse and/or dependent child, other than a former spouse and/or child for whom support is being collected, except that an additional five (5%) percent will apply if it appears that such earnings are to enforce past-due support for a period which is twelve (12) weeks or more prior to the pay period to which the offset applies.
claims.summary: The maximum part of a Federal salary payment per pay period subject to offset to collect past-due support shall not exceed the amounts set forth in section 1673(b)(2) (A) and (B) of Title 15, United States Code.

claims.quote: (2) The maximum allowable offset amount shall be reduced by the amount of any deductions in pay resulting from a garnishment order for support. Nothing in this rule is intended to alter rules applicable to processing garnishment orders for child support and/or alimony.
claims.summary: The maximum allowable offset amount shall be reduced by the amount of any deductions in pay resulting from a garnishment order for support.

claims.quote: (3) Federal salary payments subject to offset for the collection of past-due support include current basic pay, special pay, incentive pay, retainer pay, overtime, or in the case of an employee not entitled to basic pay, other authorized pay. Aggregate disposable earnings for purposes of determining the maximum amounts which may be offset under paragraph (j)(1) of this section is Federal salary pay remaining after the deduction of: (i) Any amount required by law to be withheld; (ii) Amounts properly withheld for Federal, State or local income tax purposes; (iii) Amounts deducted as health insurance premiums; (iv) Amounts deducted as normal retirement contributions, not including amounts deducted for supplementary coverage; and (v) Amounts deducted as normal life insurance premiums not including amounts deducted for supplementary coverage.
claims.summary: Federal salary payments subject to offset for the collection of past-due support include current basic pay, special pay, incentive pay, retainer pay, overtime, or other authorized pay. Aggregate disposable earnings for purposes of determining the maximum amounts which may be offset under paragraph (j)(1) of this section is Federal salary pay remaining after the deduction of specified amounts.

claims.quote: (4) At least 30 days in advance of offset, the disbursing official shall send written notice to the debtor of the maximum offset limitations described in paragraph (j)(1) of this section. The notice shall include a request that the debtor submit supporting affidavits or other documentation necessary to determine the applicable offset percentage limitation. The notice shall also inform the debtor of the percentage that will be deducted if he/she fails to submit the requested documentation.
claims.summary: At least 30 days in advance of offset, the disbursing official shall send written notice to the debtor of the maximum offset limitations described in paragraph (j)(1) of this section.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service and HHS, or the appropriate State, will adjust their debtor records accordingly.
claims.affected_party: Fiscal Service and HHS, or the appropriate State
claims.summary: Adjust debtor records accordingly.

claims.quote: A levy pursuant to the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 shall take precedence over deductions under this section.
claims.affected_party: Fiscal Service and HHS, or the appropriate State
claims.summary: A levy under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 takes precedence over deductions under this section.

claims.quote: Offsets will be applied first to past-due support being enforced by the State before any other offsets under this part.
claims.affected_party: Fiscal Service and HHS, or the appropriate State
claims.summary: Offsets will be applied first to past-due support being enforced by the State before any other offsets under this part.

claims.quote: Disbursing officials of Fiscal Service or any other disbursing official which conducts an offset will notify the payee in writing of the occurrence of the offset to satisfy past-due support.
claims.affected_party: Disbursing officials of Fiscal Service or any other disbursing official
claims.summary: Disbursing officials must notify the payee in writing of the occurrence of the offset to satisfy past-due support.

claims.quote: The notice shall inform the payee of the type and amount of the payment that was offset; the identity of the State which requested the offset; and a contact point within the State that will handle concerns regarding the offset.
claims.affected_party: Disbursing officials of Fiscal Service or any other disbursing official
claims.summary: The notice must inform the payee of the type and amount of the payment that was offset, the identity of the State which requested the offset, and a contact point within the State that will handle concerns regarding the offset.

claims.quote: Disbursing officials of Fiscal Service or any other disbursing official which conducts an offset under this section will share with HHS, upon request by the Secretary of HHS, information contained in payment certification records of persons who are delinquent in child support obligations that would assist in the collection of such debts.
claims.affected_party: Disbursing officials of Fiscal Service or any other disbursing official
claims.summary: Disbursing officials must share information contained in payment certification records of persons who are delinquent in child support obligations with HHS upon request.

claims.quote: Neither the disbursing official nor the agency authorizing the payment shall be liable for the amount of the administrative offset on the basis that the underlying obligation, represented by the payment before the administrative offset was taken, was not satisfied.
claims.affected_party: Disbursing official and agency authorizing the payment
claims.summary: Disbursing officials and the agency authorizing the payment shall not be liable for the amount of the administrative offset if the underlying obligation was not satisfied.

claims.quote: Disbursing officials will notify the agency authorizing the payment that the offset has occurred so that the agency authorizing the payment may direct any inquiries concerning the offset to the appropriate State.
claims.summary: Disbursing officials must notify the agency authorizing the payment that the offset has occurred so that the agency may direct inquiries to the appropriate State.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will ensure that an individual's Social Security number will not be visible on the outside of any package it sends by mail.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must ensure that an individual's Social Security number is not visible on the outside of any package it sends by mail.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service generally will redact or partially redact Social Security numbers in documents it sends by mail; however, to administer administrative offset, Fiscal Service (and other disbursing officials) may include Social Security numbers in mailed documents, including, for example: (1) In interoffice and interagency communications; (2) In notices, including notices to the debtor or payee that an offset has or will occur, when the Social Security number is (or is embedded in) a creditor agency's account number, debt identification number, or debtor identification number; (3) In response to a request of a debtor or a debtor's representative for records of Fiscal Service's offset activities; and (4) When required by law.
claims.affected_party: Fiscal Service and other disbursing officials
claims.summary: Fiscal Service and other disbursing officials may include Social Security numbers in mailed documents under specific circumstances, such as interoffice communications, notices about offsets, responses to requests for records, or when required by law.

claims.quote: (1) A Federal agency (as defined in 26 U.S.C. 6402(g)) that is owed by a person a past-due, legally enforceable nontax debt shall notify Fiscal Service of the amount of such debt for collection by tax refund offset.
claims.summary: A Federal agency that is owed a past-due, legally enforceable nontax debt must notify Fiscal Service of the amount of such debt for collection by tax refund offset.

claims.quote: (2) Fiscal Service will compare tax refund payment records, as certified by the IRS, with records of debts submitted to Fiscal Service. A match will occur when the taxpayer identifying number (as that term is used in 26 U.S.C. 6109) and name (or derivation of the name, known as a “name control”) of a payment certification record are the same as the taxpayer identifying number and name control of a debtor record. When a match occurs and all other requirements for tax refund offset have been met, Fiscal Service will reduce the amount of any tax refund payment payable to a debtor by the amount of any past-due, legally enforceable debt owed by the debtor.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must compare tax refund payment records with debt records and reduce tax refund payments by the amount of past-due, legally enforceable debts when a match occurs.

claims.quote: (4)(i) This section applies to Federal Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance (OASDI) overpayments provided the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 3720A(f)(1) and (2) are met with respect to such overpayments.
claims.summary: Federal agencies must ensure that the requirements of 31 U.S.C. 3720A(f)(1) and (2) are met for OASDI overpayments.

claims.quote: (c) Regulations. Prior to submitting debts to Fiscal Service for collection by tax refund offset, Federal agencies shall promulgate temporary or final regulations under 31 U.S.C. 3716 and 31 U.S.C. 3720A, governing the agencies' authority to collect debts by administrative offset, in general, and offset of tax refund payments, in particular.
claims.summary: Federal agencies must promulgate temporary or final regulations under 31 U.S.C. 3716 and 3720A before submitting debts to Fiscal Service for tax refund offset.

claims.quote: (d) Agency certification and referral of debt —(1) Past-due, legally enforceable debt eligible for tax refund offset. For purposes of this section, when a Federal agency refers a past-due, legally enforceable debt to Fiscal Service for tax refund offset, the agency will certify to Fiscal Service that: (i) The debt is past-due and legally enforceable in the amount submitted to Fiscal Service and that the agency will ensure that collections are properly credited to the debt;
claims.summary: A Federal agency must certify to Fiscal Service that the debt is past-due and legally enforceable in the amount submitted to Fiscal Service.

claims.quote: (ii) The creditor agency has made reasonable efforts to obtain payment of the debt in that the agency has: (A) Submitted the debt to Fiscal Service for collection by administrative offset and complied with the provisions of 31 U.S.C.
claims.summary: A creditor agency must have submitted the debt to Fiscal Service for collection by administrative offset and complied with the provisions of 31 U.S.C.

claims.quote: (B) Notified, or has made a reasonable attempt to notify, the debtor that the debt is past-due, and unless repaid within 60 days after the date of the notice, will be referred to Fiscal Service for tax refund offset;
claims.summary: The creditor agency must notify the debtor that the debt is past-due and will refer the debt to Fiscal Service for tax refund offset if not repaid within 60 days.

claims.quote: (C) Given the debtor at least 60 days to present evidence that all or part of the debt is not past-due or legally enforceable, considered any evidence presented by the debtor, and determined that the debt is past-due and legally enforceable;
claims.summary: The creditor agency must provide the debtor at least 60 days to present evidence that the debt is not past-due or legally enforceable, consider the evidence, and determine the debt's status.

claims.quote: (D) Provided the debtor with an opportunity to make a written agreement to repay the amount of the debt;
claims.summary: The creditor agency must provide the debtor with an opportunity to make a written agreement to repay the debt.

claims.quote: (ii) For purposes of paragraph (d)(1)(iii)(C) of this section, if the evidence presented by the debtor is considered by an agent of the creditor agency, or other entities or persons acting on the agency's behalf, the debtor must be accorded at least 30 days from the date the agent or other entity or person determines that all or part of the debt is past-due and legally enforceable to request review by an officer or employee of the agency of any unresolved dispute. The agency must then notify the debtor of its decision.
claims.summary: The debtor must be accorded at least 30 days from the date the agent or other entity determines that all or part of the debt is past-due and legally enforceable to request review by an officer or employee of the agency. The agency must notify the debtor of its decision.

claims.quote: (iii) The debt is at least $25;
claims.summary: The debt must be at least $25.

claims.quote: (3) Referral of past-due, legally enforceable debt. A Federal agency will submit past-due, legally enforceable debt information for tax refund offset to Fiscal Service in the time and manner prescribed by Fiscal Service. For each debt, the creditor agency will include the following information: (i) The name and taxpayer identifying number (as defined in 26 U.S.C. 6109) of the debtor who is responsible for the debt; (ii) The amount of such past-due and legally enforceable debt; (iii) The date on which the debt became past-due; (iv) The designation of the Federal agency or subagency referring the debt; and (v) In the case of an OASDI overpayment, a certification by the Commissioner of Social Security designating whether the amount payable to the agency is to be deposited in either the Federal Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund or the Federal Disability Insurance Trust Fund, but not both.
claims.summary: A Federal agency must submit past-due, legally enforceable debt information for tax refund offset to Fiscal Service. The creditor agency must include the debtor's name and taxpayer identifying number, the amount of the debt, the date it became past-due, the designation of the Federal agency or subagency, and in the case of an OASDI overpayment, a certification by the Commissioner of Social Security.

claims.quote: (4) Correcting and updating referral. If, after referring a past-due, legally enforceable debt to Fiscal Service as provided in paragraph (d)(3) of this section, a creditor agency determines that an error has been made with respect to the information transmitted to Fiscal Service, or if an agency receives a payment or credits a payment to the account of a debtor referred to Fiscal Service for offset, or if the debt amount is otherwise incorrect, the agency shall promptly notify Fiscal Service and make the appropriate correction of the agency's records. Creditor agencies will provide certification as required under paragraph (d)(1) of this section for any increases to amounts owed.
claims.summary: If an error is made with respect to the information transmitted to Fiscal Service, or if a payment is received or credited to the account of a debtor referred to Fiscal Service for offset, or if the debt amount is otherwise incorrect, the creditor agency must promptly notify Fiscal Service and make the appropriate correction of the agency's records. Creditor agencies must provide certification as required under paragraph (d)(1) of this section for any increases to amounts owed.

claims.quote: (5) Fiscal Service may reject a certification which does not comply with the requirements of paragraph (d)(1) of this section.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service may reject a certification that does not comply with the requirements of paragraph (d)(1) of this section.

claims.quote: Upon notification of the rejection and the reason for the rejection, a creditor agency may resubmit the debt with a corrected certification.
claims.summary: A creditor agency may resubmit the debt with a corrected certification upon notification of the rejection and the reason for the rejection.

claims.quote: Creditor agencies may submit debts to Fiscal Service for collection by tax refund offset irrespective of the amount of time the debt has been outstanding.
claims.summary: Creditor agencies may submit debts to Fiscal Service for collection by tax refund offset irrespective of the amount of time the debt has been outstanding.

claims.quote: For debts outstanding more than ten years on or before December 28, 2009, creditor agencies must certify to Fiscal Service that the notice of intent to offset described in paragraph (d)(1)(ii)(B) of this section was sent to the debtor after the debt became ten years delinquent.
claims.summary: For debts outstanding more than ten years on or before December 28, 2009, creditor agencies must certify to Fiscal Service that the notice of intent to offset described in paragraph (d)(1)(ii)(B) of this section was sent to the debtor after the debt became ten years delinquent.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will notify the payee(s) to whom the tax refund payment is due, in writing of: (A) The amount and date of the offset to satisfy a past-due, legally enforceable nontax debt; (B) The creditor agency to which this amount has been paid or credited; and (C) A contact point within the creditor agency that will handle concerns or questions regarding the offset.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service will notify the payee(s) to whom the tax refund payment is due, in writing of the amount and date of the offset to satisfy a past-due, legally enforceable nontax debt, the creditor agency to which this amount has been paid or credited, and a contact point within the creditor agency that will handle concerns or questions regarding the offset.

claims.quote: The notice in paragraph (e)(1)(i) of this section will also advise any non-debtor spouse who may have filed a joint tax return with the debtor of the steps which a non-debtor spouse may take in order to secure his or her proper share of the tax refund.
claims.summary: The notice in paragraph (e)(1)(i) of this section will also advise any non-debtor spouse who may have filed a joint tax return with the debtor of the steps which a non-debtor spouse may take in order to secure his or her proper share of the tax refund.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will advise each creditor agency of the names, mailing addresses, and identifying numbers of the debtors from whom amounts of past-due, legally enforceable debt were collected and of the amounts collected from each debtor for that agency.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service will advise each creditor agency of the names, mailing addresses, and identifying numbers of the debtors from whom amounts of past-due, legally enforceable debt were collected and of the amounts collected from each debtor for that agency.

claims.quote: At least weekly, Fiscal Service will notify the IRS of the names and taxpayer identifying numbers of the debtors from whom amounts of past-due, legally enforceable debt were collected and the amounts collected from each debtor.
claims.summary: At least weekly, Fiscal Service will notify the IRS of the names and taxpayer identifying numbers of the debtors from whom amounts of past-due, legally enforceable debt were collected and the amounts collected from each debtor.

claims.quote: If the person filing a joint return with a debtor owing the past-due, legally enforceable debt takes appropriate action to secure his or her proper share of a tax refund from which an offset was made, the IRS will pay the person his or her share of the refund and request that Fiscal Service deduct that amount from amounts payable to the creditor agency.
claims.summary: If the person filing a joint return with a debtor owing the past-due, legally enforceable debt takes appropriate action to secure his or her proper share of a tax refund from which an offset was made, the IRS will pay the person his or her share of the refund and request that Fiscal Service deduct that amount from amounts payable to the creditor agency.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will transmit amounts collected for past-due, legally enforceable debts, less fees charged under paragraph (h) of this section, to the creditor agency's account.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service will transmit amounts collected for past-due, legally enforceable debts, less fees charged under paragraph (h) of this section, to the creditor agency's account.

claims.quote: The creditor agency will reimburse Fiscal Service and the IRS for the full cost of administering the tax refund offset program.
claims.summary: The creditor agency will reimburse Fiscal Service and the IRS for the full cost of administering the tax refund offset program.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will deduct the fees from amounts collected prior to disposition and transmit a portion of the fees deducted to reimburse the IRS for its share of the cost of administering the tax refund offset program.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must deduct fees from collected amounts and transmit a portion to reimburse the IRS.

claims.quote: Any reduction of a taxpayer's refund made pursuant to 26 U.S.C. 6402(d) shall not be subject to review by any court of the United States or by the Secretary of the Treasury, Fiscal Service or IRS in an administrative proceeding.
claims.affected_party: any court of the United States, Secretary of the Treasury, Fiscal Service, IRS
claims.summary: No review of reductions made under 26 U.S.C. 6402(d) is allowed by any court, Secretary, Fiscal Service, or IRS.

claims.quote: Any action which is otherwise available with respect to recoveries of overpayments of benefits under 42 U.S.C. 404 must be taken against the Commissioner of Social Security.
claims.summary: Actions regarding overpayment recoveries under 42 U.S.C. 404 must be taken against the Commissioner of Social Security.

claims.quote: Access to and use of confidential tax information in connection with the tax refund offset program are restricted by 26 U.S.C. 6103.
claims.summary: Access to and use of confidential tax information in the tax refund offset program are restricted by 26 U.S.C. 6103.

claims.quote: agencies are subject to the safeguard, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements of 26 U.S.C. 6103(p)(4) and the regulations thereunder.
claims.summary: Agencies must comply with safeguard, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements under 26 U.S.C. 6103(p)(4) and its regulations.

claims.quote: The agency shall inform its officers and employees who access or use confidential tax information of the restrictions and penalties under the Internal Revenue Code for misuse of confidential tax information.
claims.summary: The agency must inform its officers and employees about restrictions and penalties for misuse of confidential tax information.

claims.quote: Past-due support will be collected by tax refund offset upon notification to Fiscal Service in accordance with 26 U.S.C. 6402(c), 42 U.S.C. 664 and this section.
claims.summary: Past-due support will be collected by tax refund offset upon notification to Fiscal Service in accordance with 26 U.S.C. 6402(c), 42 U.S.C. 664, and this section.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will compare tax refund payment records, as certified by the IRS, with records of debts submitted to Fiscal Service. A match will occur when the taxpayer identifying number (as that term is used in 26 U.S.C. 6109) and name of a payment certification record are the same as the taxpayer identifying number and name of a delinquent debtor record. When a match occurs and all other requirements for tax refund offset have been met, Fiscal Service will reduce the amount of any tax refund payment payable to a debtor by the amount of any past-due support debt owed by the debtor. Any amounts not offset will be paid to the payee(s) listed in the payment certification record.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must compare tax refund payment records with debt records and reduce refunds by past-due support debt when a match occurs.

claims.quote: Past-due support qualifies for tax refund offset if: (i)(A) There has been an assignment of the support obligation to a State and the amount of past-due support is not less than $25.00, or such higher amount as HHS rules may allow, whichever is greater; or (B) A State agency is providing support collection services under 42 U.S.C. 654(4) and the amount of the past-due support is not less than $500.00; and (ii) A notification of liability for past-due support has been received by Fiscal Service as prescribed by paragraphs (c)(2) or (c)(3) of this section.
claims.summary: Past-due support qualifies for tax refund offset if the amount meets specific thresholds and a notification of liability has been received by Fiscal Service.

claims.quote: States notifying HHS of past-due support shall do so in the manner and format prescribed by HHS. The notification of liability shall be accompanied by a certification that the State has complied with the requirements contained in paragraph (c)(4) of this section and with any requirements applicable to the offset of Federal tax refunds to collect past-due support imposed by State law or procedures. HHS shall consolidate and transmit to Fiscal Service the information contained in the notifications of liability for past-due support submitted by the States provided that the State has certified that the requirements of paragraph (c)(4) of this section have been met.
claims.summary: States must notify HHS of past-due support in a prescribed manner and include a certification of compliance with requirements.

claims.quote: States must notify HHS of past-due support in accordance with the provisions of paragraph (c)(2) of this section unless HHS rules authorize notification to Fiscal Service directly. If authorized by HHS rules, States may notify Fiscal Service directly of past-due support. States notifying Fiscal Service directly of past-due support shall do so in the manner and format prescribed by Fiscal Service. The notification of liability shall be accompanied by a certification that the State has complied with the requirements contained in paragraph (c)(4) of this section and with any requirements applicable to the offset of Federal tax refunds to collect past-due support imposed by State law or procedures.
claims.summary: States must notify HHS or Fiscal Service directly of past-due support in a prescribed manner and include a certification of compliance with requirements.

claims.quote: The State, or HHS if the State requests and HHS agrees, is required to provide a written notification to the debtor, pursuant to the provisions of 42 U.S.C. 664(a)(3) and 45 CFR 303.72(e), informing the debtor that the State intends to refer the debt for collection by tax refund offset.
claims.summary: The State, or HHS if requested, is required to provide a written notification to the debtor informing them of the intent to collect the debt via tax refund offset.

claims.quote: The notice also shall: (i) Instruct the debtor of the steps which may be taken to contest the State's determination that past-due support is owed or the amount of the past-due support; (ii) Advise any non-debtor who may file a joint tax return with the debtor of the steps which a non-debtor spouse may take in order to secure his or her proper share of the tax refund; and (iii) In cases when a debt is being enforced by more than one State, advise the debtor of his or her opportunities to request a review with the State enforcing collection or the State issuing the support order as prescribed by the provisions of 45 CFR 303.72(g).
claims.summary: The State must provide the debtor with instructions on contesting the determination of past-due support, advise non-debtors on securing their share of the tax refund, and inform the debtor of opportunities for review when multiple states are involved.

claims.quote: The State shall, in the manner and in the time frames provided by Fiscal Service or HHS, notify Fiscal Service or HHS of any deletion or net decrease in the amount of past-due support referred to Fiscal Service, or HHS as the case may be, for collection by tax refund offset.
claims.summary: The State must notify Fiscal Service or HHS of any deletion or net decrease in the amount of past-due support referred to them for collection by tax refund offset.

claims.quote: The State may notify Fiscal Service or HHS of any increases in the amount of the debt referred to Fiscal Service for collection by tax refund offset provided that the State has complied with the requirements of paragraph (c)(4) of this section with regard to those debts.
claims.summary: The State may notify Fiscal Service or HHS of any increases in the amount of the debt referred to Fiscal Service for collection by tax refund offset, provided that the State has complied with the requirements of paragraph (c)(4) of this section.

claims.quote: When a State has knowledge that the debt is being enforced by more than one State, the State notifying Fiscal Service, or HHS as the case may be, of the debt shall inform any such other State involved in enforcing the debt when it receives the offset amount.
claims.summary: When a State has knowledge that the debt is being enforced by more than one State, the State notifying Fiscal Service or HHS of the debt must inform any other State involved in enforcing the debt when it receives the offset amount.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service shall notify the debtor in writing of: (A) The amount and date of the offset to satisfy past-due support; (B) The State to which this amount has been paid or credited; and (C) A contact point within the State that will handle concerns or questions regarding the offset.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must notify the debtor in writing of the amount and date of the offset to satisfy past-due support, the State to which the amount has been paid or credited, and a contact point within the State to handle concerns or questions regarding the offset.

claims.quote: The notice in paragraph (e)(1)(i) of this section also will advise any non-debtor who may have filed a joint tax return with the debtor of the steps which a non-debtor spouse may take in order to secure his or her proper share of the tax refund.
claims.summary: The notice in paragraph (e)(1)(i) of this section will also advise any non-debtor who may have filed a joint tax return with the debtor of the steps which a non-debtor spouse may take to secure his or her proper share of the tax refund.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will advise HHS of the names, mailing addresses, and identifying numbers of the debtors from whom amounts of past-due support were collected, of the amounts collected from each debtor through tax refund offset, the names of any non-debtor spouses who may have filed a joint return with the debtor, and of the State on whose behalf each collection was made.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must advise HHS of the names, mailing addresses, and identifying numbers of the debtors from whom amounts of past-due support were collected, the amounts collected from each debtor through tax refund offset, the names of any non-debtor spouses who may have filed a joint return with the debtor, and the State on whose behalf each collection was made.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will inform HHS and each State that the payment source is a tax refund payment.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must inform HHS and each State that the payment source is a tax refund payment.

claims.quote: At least weekly, Fiscal Service will notify the IRS of the names and taxpayer identifying numbers of the debtors from whom amounts owed for past-due support were collected from tax refund offsets and the amounts collected from each debtor.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must notify the IRS weekly of debtors from whom past-due support was collected through tax refund offsets and the amounts collected.

claims.quote: At such time and in such manner as Fiscal Service and HHS agree, but no less than annually, Fiscal Service will advise HHS of the States which have furnished notices of past-due support, the number of cases in each State with respect to which such notices have been furnished, the amount of past-due support sought to be collected by each State, and the amount of such tax refund offset collections actually made in the case of each State.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must advise HHS annually, in a manner agreed upon, about the States that have furnished notices of past-due support, the number of cases, the amount sought to be collected, and the amount actually collected.

claims.quote: Fiscal Service will transmit amounts collected for debts, less fees charged under paragraph (i) of this section, to HHS or to the appropriate State.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must transmit amounts collected for debts, after deducting fees, to HHS or the appropriate State.

claims.quote: If IRS notifies Fiscal Service that a tax refund payment that was offset was erroneous or otherwise not due to the taxpayer, Fiscal Service will notify HHS or the appropriate State that the tax refund payment was not eligible for offset.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must notify HHS or the appropriate State if the IRS notifies them that a tax refund payment was erroneously offset.

claims.quote: HHS and States shall notify Fiscal Service any time HHS or a State returns an erroneous offset payment to an affected taxpayer.
claims.summary: HHS and States must notify Fiscal Service whenever they return an erroneous offset payment to an affected taxpayer.

claims.quote: If IRS notifies Fiscal Service on or after January 1, 2016, that a tax refund payment that was offset was erroneous or otherwise not due to the taxpayer, Fiscal Service shall not deduct the amount of the erroneous offset funds from amounts due to HHS or the State, or otherwise demand return of the offset funds from the State pursuant to paragraph (g) of this section, if the date of IRS's notification to Fiscal Service in paragraph (g) is more than six months after the date the tax refund was offset ( i.e., the tax refund payment date); and the State has already forwarded the funds as required or authorized by 42 U.S.C. 657.
claims.summary: Fiscal Service must not deduct erroneous offset funds from amounts due to HHS or the State if the IRS notifies them on or after January 1, 2016, that the offset was erroneous and the notification is more than six months after the tax refund was offset, provided the State has already forwarded the funds.

claims.quote: The State will pay a fee to Fiscal Service for the full cost of administering the tax refund offset program.
claims.summary: The State must pay a fee to Fiscal Service for the full cost of administering the tax refund offset program.

claims.quote: Fees will be charged only for actual tax refund offsets completed.
claims.summary: Fees will be charged only for actual tax refund offsets completed.

claims.quote: In accordance with 26 U.S.C. 6402(f), any reduction of a taxpayer's refund made pursuant to 26 U.S.C.
claims.summary: The IRS must comply with 26 U.S.C. 6402(f) regarding any reduction of a taxpayer's refund made pursuant to 26 U.S.C.

claims.quote: 6402(c), (d), or (e) shall not be subject to review by any court of the United States or by the Secretary of the Treasury, Fiscal Service or IRS in an administrative proceeding.
claims.summary: The reduction under 26 U.S.C. 6402(c), (d), or (e) is not subject to review by any court of the United States or by the Secretary of the Treasury, Fiscal Service, or IRS in an administrative proceeding.

claims.quote: No action brought against the United States to recover the amount of this reduction shall be considered to be a suit for refund of tax.
claims.summary: No action brought against the United States to recover the amount of this reduction shall be considered to be a suit for refund of tax.

claims.quote: Access to and use of confidential tax information in connection with the tax refund offset program is permitted to the extent necessary in establishing appropriate agency records, locating any person with respect to whom a reduction under 26 U.S.C. 6402(c) is sought for purposes of collecting the debt, and in the defense of any litigation or administrative procedure ensuing from a reduction made under section 6402(c).
claims.summary: Access to and use of confidential tax information in connection with the tax refund offset program is permitted to the extent necessary in establishing appropriate agency records, locating any person with respect to whom a reduction under 26 U.S.C. 6402(c) is sought for purposes of collecting the debt, and in the defense of any litigation or administrative procedure ensuing from a reduction made under section 6402(c).

claims.quote: This section applies to tax refund payments payable under 26 U.S.C. 6402 after January 1, 1999.
claims.summary: This section applies to tax refund payments payable under 26 U.S.C. 6402 after January 1, 1999.
